title: Asking for Travel Information
description: Request and clarify times, platforms, locations, and prices.
objectives: Request and clarify times, platforms, locations, and prices.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to request and clarify times, platforms, locations, and prices. The central language is indirect polite questions with could and can. It belongs to the practical context of travel & accommodation. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: indirect polite questions with could and can

blocks.english: Could you tell me when the train leaves?
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the asking for travel information exchange.

blocks.english: Do you know which platform I need?
blocks.explanation: This asking for travel information model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: Could you help me with this problem?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the asking for travel information exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Could you tell me when the train leaves?” and “Do you know which platform I need?” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: indirect polite questions with could and can.
